chunk_findings.detail: `install` uses a prior worktree `core.hooksPath` value directly as a filesystem path (`original = Path(prior.out.strip())`) and then decides whether to wrap other hooks with `if original.is_dir()`. Git resolves a relative `core.hooksPath` against the worktree top-level, but `Path.is_dir()` resolves against the Python process cwd. For example, if the lane worktree has `git config --worktree core.hooksPath .githooks` and ddflow is invoked from a different cwd, the loop is skipped, so hooks such as `.githooks/commit-msg` are not wrapped; after `core.hooksPath` is changed to the lane directory, those project hooks silently no longer run. If a same-named directory exists in the process cwd, the wrong hooks are wrapped instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: The loop over `original.iterdir()` wraps every regular non-sample file regardless of executable bit. Git ignores non-executable hooks, but `_write_exec` makes the wrapper executable and its body unconditionally `exec`s the original file. If a project disables a hook by leaving it non-executable, e.g. `.git/hooks/pre-push` with mode `0644`, installing the lane hook creates an executable `pre-push` wrapper; `git push` then runs the wrapper, and because the target is not executable the shell exits with 126 (or the disabled hook unexpectedly runs), changing push behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: `uninstall` removes the lane override by running `git config --worktree --unset core.hooksPath` instead of restoring the saved original. If the worktree already had a non-default worktree `core.hooksPath` before install, e.g. `/custom/hooks`, install chains and saves that path, but uninstall unsets the key and deletes `d/original`, leaving `/custom/hooks` no longer configured. This contradicts the stated “uninstall restores the worktree’s setting” behavior and silently drops the prior hooks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:uninstall

chunk_findings.detail: If the hook is reinstalled while `core.hooksPath` already points to the lane directory but `d/original` is missing, or if the prior value is an alias such as a trailing-slash path to the same directory, `original` can become `_current_hooks_path(worktree)`, which resolves to the lane hook directory because it respects `core.hooksPath`. `render(chain_to=original)` then emits `[ -x <lane-dir>/pre-commit ] && exec <lane-dir>/pre-commit "$@"`; after the lease check passes or fails open, the generated hook execs itself, so a clean `git commit` loops forever instead of completing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: `install` never removes wrappers left in `d` from a previous state. If the lane was installed when the original hooks directory contained `commit-msg`, and the project later removes or moves that hook, a subsequent `install` does not delete `d/commit-msg`. Git then runs the stale wrapper, whose `exec` target no longer exists, causing the commit to fail even though the project no longer has a `commit-msg` hook.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: The tests are not isolated from the user’s global/system Git configuration. Line 52 uses `git config --get core.hooksPath`, which reports the effective value, not the local repo value. If the environment has, for example, `git config --global core.hooksPath /some/hooks`, then `sh(main, "git", "config", "--get", "core.hooksPath", check=False).stdout` is `/some/hooks\n` and the assertion fails even though the lane install did not touch the primary checkout’s local config. The same lack of isolation also affects `test_the_projects_own_hooks_still_run`: with a global `core.hooksPath`, Git will not execute the hook written to `main/.git/hooks/pre-commit`, so line 104 fails. A global `commit.gpgsign=true` can also make the fixture’s `git commit` fail. The fixture should isolate config (e.g. `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`) and the assertion should use `--local` when checking that the repo-local setting is untouched.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The “without leaking” test only checks `r.stderr`, but the stubs deliberately write the secret to stdout: `echo 'Traceback: token= [REDACTED] exit 1` and `echo boom SECRET123; exit 127`. If the installed hook script forwards the invocation’s stdout to the hook’s stdout, `git commit` can emit `SECRET123` on `r.stdout`, yet this test still passes because line 77 and line 80 only assert `"SECRET123" not in r.stderr`. Given that the stub output is the leak vector, the test should assert `"SECRET123" not in r.stdout` (or check combined output) to actually enforce the “without leaking” property.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:77

chunk_findings.detail: `install` points the worktree’s `core.hooksPath` at a directory containing a snapshot of the original hooks: it writes one wrapper for every executable file that exists in the original hooks directory at install time. Git therefore runs only those wrappers. If the project later adds a hook, e.g. `commit-msg` appears in the original hooks directory after the lane hook was installed, there is no wrapper for it and commits in that lane silently skip the new project check. Conversely, if a wrapped hook is removed or made non-executable after install, the stale wrapper remains; when Git runs it, the wrapper executes `exec /original/commit-msg "$@"`, the exec fails with 127/126, and the commit/push is aborted. This contradicts the module’s claim that installing the lane hook removes no project check and fails open.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: `install` is documented as idempotent, but a second install changes what `uninstall` restores. On a clean worktree, the first install writes `had_prior=0`. On a second install, the current worktree `core.hooksPath` is already the lane directory, so `had_prior` is computed true; the stale-cleanup loop deletes the old `had_prior` file before `_had_prior(d)` can read it, so the flag is written as `1`. `uninstall` then takes the `had_prior` branch and sets the worktree’s `core.hooksPath` to the saved original instead of unsetting it. Thus `install(); install(); uninstall()` leaves a worktree `core.hooksPath` on a worktree that originally had none; if the project later changes its shared `core.hooksPath`, the stale worktree value overrides it and commits use the wrong hooks directory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: `uninstall` returns early when the lane hook directory does not exist, even if the worktree’s `core.hooksPath` still points to that directory. For example, after installing the lane hook, remove the `ddflow-lane-hooks` directory manually or leave it deleted by a failed cleanup; calling `uninstall` returns “no lane hook installed” and never unsets or restores the config. Subsequent `git commit` in that worktree uses the missing `core.hooksPath`, suppressing the project’s default/shared hooks instead of restoring them. The function should check `installed(worktree)` before deciding that no lane hook is present.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:uninstall

chunk_findings.detail: `_isolated_git` is not hermetic with respect to Git repository-location environment variables. It only overrides `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, leaving `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, and related variables inherited. For example, running the tests with `GIT_DIR=[REDACTED:path]` causes `sh(main, "git", "init", ...)`, `git worktree add`, and subsequent commits to operate against that external repository (or fail against it) instead of the temporary `main`/`lane` repositories, so the tests are environment-dependent and can mutate an unrelated repo.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:13

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert d.is_dir() and "worktrees" in str(d)` can pass for a non-lane-private hook directory. If the test is run with a temp base path containing the word `worktrees` (e.g. `TMPDIR=/tmp/worktrees` or `pytest --basetemp=/tmp/worktrees`), then a path such as `/tmp/worktrees/main/.git/hooks` contains `"worktrees"` even though it is the shared primary checkout hook directory, not a per-worktree hook directory under `.git/worktrees/<name>`. Thus the test can falsely certify lane privacy.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:56

chunk_findings.detail: The output path is interpolated into the generated shell stub without quoting. If `tmp_path` contains spaces, e.g. `TMPDIR='/tmp/space dir'`, the generated line becomes `echo "$DDFLOW_ENFORCE_COMMIT_WITHOUT_LEASE $DDFLOW_AGENT" > /tmp/space dir/test_policy0/env.txt`, which the shell parses as redirection to `/tmp/space` plus an extra argument to `echo`. The expected `env.txt` is not written correctly, so the test fails even if the hook exports the variables correctly.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:98

chunk_findings.detail: `GIT_HOOKS` omits `pre-merge-commit`, a standard client-side Git hook. With an existing executable `.git/hooks/pre-merge-commit` in the original hooks directory, `install` sets `core.hooksPath` to the lane directory `d`, which contains no `pre-merge-commit` wrapper. `git merge` will then create a merge commit without running the project’s `pre-merge-commit` check, contradicting the stated “installing it removes no check” contract and allowing a pre-merge validation bypass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:GIT_HOOKS

chunk_findings.detail: `GIT_HOOKS` claims to list git’s other client-side hook names, but it omits `pre-merge-commit` and `fsmonitor-watchman`. If a project has an executable `pre-merge-commit` in its original hooks directory, installing the lane hook sets `core.hooksPath` to the lane directory, creates no `pre-merge-commit` wrapper, and a merge commit that would normally run the project’s `pre-merge-commit` check silently skips it. The same applies to an executable `fsmonitor-watchman` hook: it is not wrapped and therefore is not run through the lane `core.hooksPath`, contradicting the stated “installing it removes no check” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:GIT_HOOKS

chunk_findings.detail: When `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` is unavailable or fails, `_original` falls back to `base / ".git" / "hooks"`. For a linked worktree, `<worktree>/.git` is a file, not the common git directory, so the fallback produces an invalid hooks path such as `/lane/.git/hooks`. This occurs on Git versions that support `git config --worktree` but not `--path-format=absolute` (e.g. Git 2.20–2.30): install can set the worktree `core.hooksPath`, but the generated wrappers point at nonexistent files, so the project’s normal hooks are silently skipped even though they exist in the real common `.git/hooks` directory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:_original

chunk_findings.detail: `uninstall` ignores the result of `git config --worktree ...` when restoring or unsetting `core.hooksPath`, then deletes the lane hook directory and returns success anyway. If the config write fails, for example because the worktree config file is unwritable or invalid, the command can leave `core.hooksPath` still pointing at `ddflow-lane-hooks` while `uninstall` has deleted that directory. Subsequent commits then use a missing hooks directory and skip the project’s default/shared hooks, despite the module claiming uninstall restores the worktree setting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:uninstall

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that uninstall restores the absolute path `str(mine)` even though the prior configuration written at line 162 is the relative string `.githooks`. Git stores and returns `core.hooksPath` verbatim, so a correct “restore” should leave the worktree config as `.githooks`. This assertion therefore rejects a correct verbatim restore and certifies an implementation that rewrites the user’s configuration to an absolute path. Concrete scenario: set worktree `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks`, install and uninstall the lane hook, then move the worktree (e.g. `git worktree move`); the restored absolute path `/tmp/.../lane/.githooks` becomes stale, so Git no longer finds the project’s prior hook directory and silently skips its hooks.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:166

chunk_findings.detail: The missing-directory case does not verify that `core.hooksPath` is unset or restored. After `shutil.rmtree(GH.hook_dir(wt))`, it only checks that `uninstall` says “removed” and that `GH.installed(wt)` is false. If `uninstall` returns “removed” when the lane hook directory is missing but leaves the worktree’s `core.hooksPath` pointing at that deleted directory, this test still passes because `installed` can be false merely due to the missing directory. The next `git commit` in that worktree would then use a nonexistent hooks path and bypass all project hooks, which is the removable/fail-open behavior the test name claims to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:210

chunk_findings.detail: The loop unconditionally writes an executable `pre-merge-commit` wrapper even when the original hooks directory has no executable `pre-merge-commit`. Git uses `pre-merge-commit` for merge commits when that hook exists, and only falls back to `pre-commit` when `pre-merge-commit` is absent. After the lane hook is installed, a `git merge` in the lane worktree sees the generated `pre-merge-commit` wrapper, runs it, and because the original `pre-merge-commit` is not executable the wrapper exits 0. The merge commit is therefore created without running the lane `pre-commit` lease check (or the project’s `pre-commit` fallback), bypassing lease enforcement for merge commits. This is a new bypass introduced by adding `pre-merge-commit` to `GIT_HOOKS` without special-casing the “absent means fall back to `pre-commit`” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install (GIT_HOOKS wrapper loop, around line 149)

chunk_findings.detail: The same loop unconditionally writes an executable `push-to-checkout` wrapper even when the original hooks directory has none. For a non-bare lane worktree configured so that pushes update the worktree (e.g. `receive.denyCurrentBranch=updateInstead`), Git invokes `push-to-checkout` if it exists and, on exit status 0, assumes the hook updated the worktree and index instead of performing the default update. The generated wrapper finds no original executable hook and exits 0, so `git push` to that worktree can report success while leaving the worktree and index unchanged. Before installing the lane hook, the absence of `push-to-checkout` caused Git to use its default update path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install (GIT_HOOKS wrapper loop, around line 149)

chunk_findings.detail: The change claims to preserve the project’s existing hooks, but the earlier omission of `pre-merge-commit` is not addressed by this diff or its tests. `test_the_projects_own_hooks_still_run` only exercises `pre-commit` and `commit-msg`; no test creates an executable `pre-merge-commit` hook and attempts a merge commit. If `.git/hooks/pre-merge-commit` exists and exits 1, `GH.install(wt)` replaces `core.hooksPath` with the lane hook directory. Because the generated wrapper set does not include `pre-merge-commit`, `git merge --no-ff` can create a merge commit without running that project check, violating the “installing it removes no check” contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:GIT_HOOKS

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback for an unavailable `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` is `base / ".git"`, where `base` is the worktree top returned by `rev-parse --show-toplevel`. On a linked worktree, `<worktree>/.git` is a file, not the common git directory, so this fallback produces an invalid hooks path. On Git versions where `git config --worktree` works but `--path-format=absolute` does not (the case this fallback is written for, e.g. Git 2.20–2.30), take a linked worktree `/lane` of `/repo` with no worktree/local/global/system `core.hooksPath` and an executable `/repo/.git/hooks/pre-commit`. `install()` computes `original=/lane/.git/hooks`, writes the lane `pre-commit` to chain to `/lane/.git/hooks/pre-commit`, and writes wrappers targeting `/lane/.git/hooks/<hook>`. Those paths do not exist, so the project's default hooks are silently skipped even though the lane hook is installed, violating the stated guarantee that installing the hook removes no project checks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:_original

chunk_findings.detail: `installed()` decides whether the lane hook is in effect by comparing the raw value of worktree `core.hooksPath` to the absolute `hook_dir` string, but Git accepts equivalent values that resolve to the same hooks directory. For example, after installing the lane hook, set the worktree setting to a relative path that resolves to it: `git config --worktree core.hooksPath .git/ddflow-lane-hooks` (or an absolute path with a trailing slash/symlink equivalent). `installed(worktree)` returns false because the strings differ. `uninstall(worktree)` then skips the restore/unset branch because `installed` is false, deletes the lane hook directory, and returns success, leaving `core.hooksPath` pointing at a directory that no longer exists. The next `git commit` in that worktree finds no hooks directory and skips the project's hooks, despite the hook being effectively configured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:installed/uninstall

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to prove the lane hook is removable, but it never checks that the worktree `core.hooksPath` setting is cleared after `GH.uninstall(wt)`. It only asserts that `GH.installed(wt)` is false, that the lane hook directory no longer exists, and that a second uninstall reports “no lane hook installed”. Since `installed` can be false merely because the lane directory was deleted, an implementation whose `uninstall` removes the directory but leaves `core.hooksPath` pointing at that directory would still pass this test. A subsequent `git commit` in that worktree would then use a missing hooks directory and skip the project’s normal hooks, which is exactly the failure mode the “removable” test is supposed to catch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:test_install_is_lane_private_and_removable

chunk_findings.detail: The generated `pre-merge-commit` wrapper invokes the lane `pre-commit` script, and that script unconditionally chains to the original `pre-commit` hook. Git’s documented behavior is that when an executable `pre-merge-commit` hook exists, it is used instead of `pre-commit`. Thus, if the project’s original hooks directory contains both an executable `pre-merge-commit` that succeeds and an executable `pre-commit` that rejects merge commits, `git merge` succeeds before install but aborts after install: the wrapper runs the lane `pre-commit`, which execs the original `pre-commit` and returns its failure, so the wrapper exits nonzero before the project’s `pre-merge-commit` is reached. This adds a hook run that Git would not run and can break merge commits that previously succeeded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install (MERGE_HOOK wrapper)

chunk_findings.detail: `uninstall` restores a prior worktree `core.hooksPath` only when the saved `prior_raw` value is truthy after `.strip()`. If the worktree previously had the setting set to an empty string (`git config --worktree core.hooksPath ""`), `install` records `had_prior=1` and an empty `prior_raw`, but `uninstall` falls through to `git config --worktree --unset core.hooksPath`. That changes the configuration from “empty hooks path” to unset/default hooks; if the empty value was used to suppress hooks, hooks that were previously suppressed become active. The same loss occurs for a whitespace-only path because of `.strip()`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:uninstall

chunk_findings.detail: `install` decides whether the current worktree hooks path is already the lane directory by exact text comparison (`cur.out.strip() != str(d)`), while `installed()` compares resolved paths. If the same lane directory is spelled differently, for example with a trailing slash or as a relative path such as `.git/ddflow-lane-hooks/`, reinstall treats it as a prior setting and stores that lane-dir value in `prior_raw`, overwriting any saved prior path. A subsequent `uninstall` then restores that lane-dir value and deletes the directory, leaving `core.hooksPath` pointing at a nonexistent hooks directory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: The `pre-merge-commit` wrapper is written unconditionally and only execs `original/pre-merge-commit`; it never falls back to `original/pre-commit`. Git runs the `pre-commit` hook for a merge commit when there is no executable `pre-merge-commit` hook. Given a repository whose chained hooks directory contains `pre-commit` but no `pre-merge-commit`, installing the lane hook creates an executable lane `pre-merge-commit`. On `git merge --no-ff`, Git runs the lane wrapper instead of falling back to `pre-commit`; if the lane lease check passes, the wrapper finds no executable `original/pre-merge-commit` and exits 0, so the project's own `pre-commit` hook is skipped. This contradicts the stated intent that the project's hooks are still run and can silently bypass project checks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install (MERGE_HOOK branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The crash detection treats any normal exit status 1 output containing the literal string `Traceback (most recent call last)` as a crash and allows the commit. This makes the fail-open condition triggerable by non-crash output. For example, if the lease checker prints an offending path and an agent commits a file outside the lease named `Traceback (most recent call last)`, the captured output contains that string, the `case` matches, the hook prints “the lease check crashed; commit allowed”, does not exit 1, and the out-of-lease commit is allowed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:_SCRIPT

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to prove that the primary checkout is untouched, but it only checks `core.hooksPath` in `main`’s `--local` config. If `GH.install(wt)` incorrectly wrote the lane hooks path globally (`git config --global core.hooksPath <lane-hook-dir>`) or into `main`’s own worktree config, `main` commits would be affected by the lane hook, yet `sh(main, "git", "config", "--local", "--get", "core.hooksPath")` would still return empty and the test would pass. The lane-private assertion therefore has a concrete false negative: a global/worktree-level leak on the primary checkout is not detected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:test_install_is_lane_private_and_removable

chunk_findings.detail: The uninstall check `got = sh(wt, "git", "config", "--worktree", "--get", "core.hooksPath", check=False); assert got.stdout == ""` treats any failed `git config` as “cleared”. For example, if `git config --worktree --get core.hooksPath` exits 128 with empty stdout because `--worktree` is unsupported in that Git build, `config.worktree` is corrupt, or the option requires an extension that is not enabled, the assertion passes even though it has not proven that the setting is absent. The same pattern appears in `test_install_twice_then_uninstall_unsets_and_a_missing_dir_still_restores` and `test_installed_and_uninstall_accept_an_equivalent_spelling`; the tests should at least reject fatal return codes rather than only looking at stdout.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:test_install_is_lane_private_and_removable

chunk_findings.detail: After removing both `push-to-checkout` and `fsmonitor-watchman` from the project hooks and reinstalling, the test only asserts that the `push-to-checkout` wrapper is gone. If the implementation leaves a stale `fsmonitor-watchman` wrapper in the lane hook directory, Git could still invoke it when fsmonitor is enabled, but this test would pass. The earlier part of the same test asserts that both wrappers are created, so the removal assertion should cover both names.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:test_presence_sensitive_hooks_are_wrapped_only_when_the_project_has_one

Thus, if the project’s original hooks directory contains both an executable `pre-merge-commit` that succeeds and an executable `pre-commit` that rejects merge commits, `git merge` succeeds before install but aborts after install: the wrapper runs the lane `pre-commit`, which execs the original `pre-commit` and returns its failure, so the wrapper exits nonzero before the project’s `pre-merge-commit` is reached. This adds a hook run that Git would not run and can break merge commits that previously succeeded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install (MERGE_HOOK wrapper)

chunk_findings.detail: `uninstall` restores a prior worktree `core.hooksPath` only when the saved `prior_raw` value is truthy after `.strip()`. If the worktree previously had the setting set to an empty string (`git config --worktree core.hooksPath ""`), `install` records `had_prior=1` and an empty `prior_raw`, but `uninstall` falls through to `git config --worktree --unset core.hooksPath`. That changes the configuration from “empty hooks path” to unset/default hooks; if the empty value was used to suppress hooks, hooks that were previously suppressed become active. The same loss occurs for a whitespace-only path because of `.strip()`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:uninstall

chunk_findings.detail: `install` decides whether the current worktree hooks path is already the lane directory by exact text comparison (`cur.out.strip() != str(d)`), while `installed()` compares resolved paths. If the same lane directory is spelled differently, for example with a trailing slash or as a relative path such as `.git/ddflow-lane-hooks/`, reinstall treats it as a prior setting and stores that lane-dir value in `prior_raw`, overwriting any saved prior path. A subsequent `uninstall` then restores that lane-dir value and deletes the directory, leaving `core.hooksPath` pointing at a nonexistent hooks directory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: The `pre-merge-commit` wrapper is written unconditionally and only execs `original/pre-merge-commit`; it never falls back to `original/pre-commit`. Git runs the `pre-commit` hook for a merge commit when there is no executable `pre-merge-commit` hook. Given a repository whose chained hooks directory contains `pre-commit` but no `pre-merge-commit`, installing the lane hook creates an executable lane `pre-merge-commit`. On `git merge --no-ff`, Git runs the lane wrapper instead of falling back to `pre-commit`; if the lane lease check passes, the wrapper finds no executable `original/pre-merge-commit` and exits 0, so the project's own `pre-commit` hook is skipped. This contradicts the stated intent that the project's hooks are still run and can silently bypass project checks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install (MERGE_HOOK branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The crash detection treats any normal exit status 1 output containing the literal string `Traceback (most recent call last)` as a crash and allows the commit. This makes the fail-open condition triggerable by non-crash output. For example, if the lease checker prints an offending path and an agent commits a file outside the lease named `Traceback (most recent call last)`, the captured output contains that string, the `case` matches, the hook prints “the lease check crashed; commit allowed”, does not exit 1, and the out-of-lease commit is allowed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:_SCRIPT

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to prove that the primary checkout is untouched, but it only checks `core.hooksPath` in `main`’s `--local` config. If `GH.install(wt)` incorrectly wrote the lane hooks path globally (`git config --global core.hooksPath <lane-hook-dir>`) or into `main`’s own worktree config, `main` commits would be affected by the lane hook, yet `sh(main, "git", "config", "--local", "--get", "core.hooksPath")` would still return empty and the test would pass. The lane-private assertion therefore has a concrete false negative: a global/worktree-level leak on the primary checkout is not detected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:test_install_is_lane_private_and_removable

chunk_findings.detail: The uninstall check `got = sh(wt, "git", "config", "--worktree", "--get", "core.hooksPath", check=False); assert got.stdout == ""` treats any failed `git config` as “cleared”. For example, if `git config --worktree --get core.hooksPath` exits 128 with empty stdout because `--worktree` is unsupported in that Git build, `config.worktree` is corrupt, or the option requires an extension that is not enabled, the assertion passes even though it has not proven that the setting is absent. The same pattern appears in `test_install_twice_then_uninstall_unsets_and_a_missing_dir_still_restores` and `test_installed_and_uninstall_accept_an_equivalent_spelling`; the tests should at least reject fatal return codes rather than only looking at stdout.

chunk_findings.detail: After removing both `push-to-checkout` and `fsmonitor-watchman` from the project hooks and reinstalling, the test only asserts that the `push-to-checkout` wrapper is gone. If the implementation leaves a stale `fsmonitor-watchman` wrapper in the lane hook directory, Git could still invoke it when fsmonitor is enabled, but this test would pass. The earlier part of the same test asserts that both wrappers are created, so the removal assertion should cover both names.

chunk_findings.detail: When no `core.hooksPath` is configured in the worktree/local/global/system scopes, `_original` falls back to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`/hooks. For a linked worktree, the default hooks directory is the per-worktree `$GIT_DIR/hooks` (e.g. `.git/worktrees/<name>/hooks`), not `common/.git/hooks`. With a linked lane worktree that has its own executable `$GIT_DIR/hooks/pre-commit`, install chains to `common/.git/hooks/pre-commit` instead, so that per-worktree project hook no longer runs. The unused `_current_hooks_path` helper already uses `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`, which would return the correct effective default path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:_original

chunk_findings.detail: If the worktree initially had a prior `core.hooksPath` (say `/old`), then `install` records `had_prior=1` and `prior_raw=/old`. The generated help text says an alternative removal is `git config --worktree --unset core.hooksPath`; doing that leaves the lane directory and these files behind. A later `install` then sees `cur.ok` false but `_had_prior(d)` true, reuses the stale `d/original` and `prior_raw` `/old`, and still records `had_prior=1`, even though the actual pre-install state at that point is unset. A subsequent `uninstall` will restore `/old`, not the user’s unset state, re-introducing hooks the user had removed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: A hook file created at `main/.git/hooks` is not the lane worktree’s original hook. In a linked worktree, Git resolves default hooks under `$GIT_DIR/hooks`, which is `main/.git/worktrees/lane/hooks`, not the primary checkout’s `main/.git/hooks`; the test suite’s own `test_install_is_lane_private_and_removable` expects the lane hook dir to live under `/.git/worktrees/`. So in the fallback test, the exit-7 `main/.git/hooks/pre-commit` is inactive in `wt` before `GH.install`; a correct install that chained `wt`’s actual original hook directory would not run it, and the generated `pre-merge-commit` would instead run the lease stub (`exit 0`) and return 0, making `returncode == 7` fail. This means the tests encode the wrong “project hooks” location and do not actually reproduce the previous finding #1 merge-hook conflict scenario.

chunk_findings.detail: The fail-open crash detection only matches when the captured output begins exactly with `Traceback (most recent call last)`. If the lease-check command emits any line before the traceback (for example a log line, warning, or status message written to stderr/stdout), the command substitution puts that line first, `rc` is `1`, the inner `case` does not match the traceback pattern, and the hook executes `printf ... >&2; exit 1`. Thus a crash that prints anything before its traceback blocks the commit and also prints the traceback, contradicting the module’s stated behavior (“a crash … allows the commit” and “never the traceback”). For example, an invocation equivalent to `sh -c 'echo info >&2; echo "Traceback (most recent call last):" >&2; exit 1'` causes the lane pre-commit hook to exit 1 instead of allowing the commit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:_SCRIPT

chunk_findings.detail: Presence-sensitive hook wrappers are only written if the original hook is executable at install time, but the code comment claims hooks added or removed later are honoured at run time. If a lane is installed when the project has no executable `push-to-checkout`, and the project later adds one, the lane hook directory still contains no `push-to-checkout`; because the worktree’s `core.hooksPath` points at the lane directory, Git will not run the newly added project hook. Conversely, if the project has `push-to-checkout` when the lane is installed and later removes it without reinstalling the lane hook, the stale lane wrapper remains and exits 0; Git treats a successful `push-to-checkout` hook as having updated the working tree, so the normal default checkout is skipped. This can silently suppress or change project checks after install.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:install

chunk_findings.detail: `GIT_HOOKS` omits server-side hook names `pre-receive`, `update`, and `post-receive`, even though it includes other server-side hooks such as `post-update`. If a repository has an `update` hook and someone pushes to the lane worktree, Git uses the lane’s `core.hooksPath`; since no lane wrapper is written for `update`, the project’s `update` hook is not executed, allowing pushes that the project hook would reject. The same applies to missing `pre-receive` and `post-receive` wrappers, so the claim that installing the lane hook “removes no check” is false for those hook names.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/githook.py:GIT_HOOKS

chunk_findings.detail: This test only proves that the lane `pre-merge-commit` wrapper ultimately returns the project `pre-commit` exit status; it does not prove that the lease-check invocation runs on the fallback path. The installed invocation is `exit 0`, and the assertion is only `returncode == 7` from the project `pre-commit`. If the wrapper, when there is no project `pre-merge-commit` but there is a project `pre-commit`, execs `original/pre-commit` before running the lease check, the test still passes (final rc 7) even though merge commits would bypass the lease check. The companion test that proves the lease check runs does so with no project `pre-commit`, so it does not cover this fallback path. A failing or marker-printing invocation plus an assertion that the marker/blocking occurred is needed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_githook.py:test_merge_commit_falls_back_to_the_projects_pre_commit_without_a_merge_hook

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture isolates Git environment variables but does not remove `DDFLOW_ENFORCE_COMMIT_WITHOUT_LEASE` or `DDFLOW_AGENT` from the ambient environment. If a developer or CI environment already has `DDFLOW_ENFORCE_COMMIT_WITHOUT_LEASE=block` and `DDFLOW_AGENT=lane-1`, the stub inherits those values and the test passes even if `GH.install` does not export the policy or agent. Concrete false pass: run the test with `DDFLOW_AGENT=lane-1 DDFLOW_ENFORCE_COMMIT_WITHOUT_LEASE=block` while using an implementation that omits the exports; the stub still writes `block lane-1`.

Fixes bug Bf797745b5a: For a 10 KB module, 4 review rounds (15-25 min each, two reviewers) kept returning new MEDIUM findings on increasingly exotic cases (git 2.20 compat, path spellings, empty-string config), several against a stale head, so rubber_duck/critic stay failed with rounds exhausted. Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bf797745b5a --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bf797745b5a --regression-test <test>` first).
